I am 50, been farming this land for 20 years. My husband helps some but my older boy works in the city now, sends money home. Primary school is all I finished, but I know my fields. 10.9 mu is not small, not big either — enough to feed us and sell some.

I plant wheat in October, then maize right after wheat harvest in June. Same as everyone in our village. Same as my mother did.

For wheat: I use the improved seed from the agro-station, "Jimai" kind. Costs more but the grain is fuller. I spread about 2 bags of compound fertilizer (that 15-15-15 one) before plowing — that is 100 jin, so 50 kg per mu maybe. Then in spring when the wheat turns green, I topdress with urea, about 30 jin per mu. I water 3 times — before winter, at jointing, and when grain is filling. Our well is good, no problem. Spray pesticide 2 times, once for aphids, once for the rust if I see yellow spots. Plow with the rented tractor. Last year I got about 450 kg per mu, hoping same this year.

For maize: After wheat I do no-till, just plant straight through the stubble. Everyone does it now, saves time and the machine is cheap to rent. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan or whatever the dealer has good stock of. Put compound fertilizer with the seed, then topdress urea when the maize is knee-high — maize is hungry, needs more than wheat. I water 2 times if the rain is poor. Spray once for the borer worm. Last year about 550 kg per mu.

I do not want to cut fertilizer. Grain price is not high but losing yield is worse. My neighbor tried less fertilizer two years ago, her wheat was thin, she regretted it.
